name: 2234-unrelated-rule
defect: Unrelated behaviour change: protected internal members now require a partial formatter type

commit.author: Stelian Vultur
commit.message: Implementation for #2234 The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.summary: The analyzer regressed after version 3.1.0: starting with 3.1.1, it stops working when SuppressSourceGeneration is set to true.

criteria.text: The analyzer performs its normal analysis when SuppressSourceGeneration=true, restoring the working behavior observed in version 3.1.0.
criteria.summary: Analyzer runs normal analysis when SuppressSourceGeneration=true, matching 3.1.0 behavior

requirement.short: Analyzer must work with SuppressSourceGeneration set to true

hunks.context: This code generation has a minor upfront performance cost.
lines: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
+A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
+No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
+The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
+- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
+- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
+- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

+The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.
+                            continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
+                            continue; // The key kind does not match the other members; the diagnostic is reported, so skip this member.
-    private static bool IsPartialTypeRequired(Accessibility accessibility) => accessibility is not (Accessibility.Public or Accessibility.Internal or Accessibility.ProtectedOrInternal);
+    private static bool IsPartialTypeRequired(Accessibility accessibility) => accessibility is not (Accessibility.Public or Accessibility.Internal);

+/// A type that opts out of source generation (https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2234).
+/// It must still serialize correctly through the run-time (dynamic) resolver.
+    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
+        var value = new SuppressedSourceGenerationType { Id = 7, Name = "seven" };
+// Copyright (c) All contributors. All rights reserved.
+// Licensed under the MIT license. See LICENSE file in the project root for full license information.
+/// Verifies that the analyzer keeps validating <c>[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]</c> types
+/// Opting out of source generation only skips generation; the type is still serialized at run time, so its contract must still be checked.
+        // The partial-class requirement (MsgPack011) and the AOT-only checks (MsgPack016, MsgPack017)
+        // only matter when a formatter is generated, so they are not reported for a suppressed type.
+    public string Prop1 { get; init; } = ""some default"";

suspicions.hypothesis: Continuing immediately after a mixed-key diagnostic may skip other validation for that member; for example, a suppressed type whose string-keyed member in an integer-keyed contract also has an unsupported member type could lose its MsgPack003 diagnostic.

Retaining only the first duplicate-key member may prevent the analyzer exception but still let source generation consume an incomplete model; running the generator, not just the analyzer verifier, on a non-suppressed type with duplicate keys could expose a later failure or declaration-order-dependent output.
A nested protected internal MessagePackObject that previously did not require partial may now receive the partial-type diagnostic; none of the new tests exercises ProtectedOrInternal accessibility.
The README's claim that MsgPack012 remains active for suppressed types is not covered by a new test, so an inaccessible suppressed type could still evade that documented check.

probes.title: Mixed key kinds on a suppressed member still runs MsgPack003 validation
probes.hypothesis: H2/H5's `continue` after DoNotMixStringAndIntKeys skips the rest of the loop body for that member, so an unsupported member type on the mismatched-key member loses its MsgPack003 diagnostic even though the requirement says the analyzer does its normal analysis.
criteria: MsgPack003 is still reported on the mismatched-key member's unsupported type
probes.means: If the test fails (no MsgPack003 on Member2), the `continue` in the mixed-key branch suppresses MsgPack003, contradicting the README/requirement that MsgPack003 still applies to suppressed types.

refusals.question: Is it intended that SuppressSourceGeneration=true suppresses MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017 while retaining the listed runtime-contract diagnostics?
refusals.why: The requirement says to restore normal analyzer analysis but does not explicitly define which diagnostics are generation-only; this decides an ambiguous requirement and intentionally changes which diagnostics are reported.
refusals.summary: Decide whether SuppressSourceGeneration=true suppresses MsgPack011, MsgPack016, and MsgPack017

refusals.question: For duplicate keys, is first-member-wins collection the intended recovery for ordinary generated types as well as suppressed types, rather than stopping collection after the duplicate-key diagnostic?
refusals.why: The guards change behavior for both collection paths and allow later processing to use an incomplete, declaration-order-dependent model; choosing that intentional behavior change is left to the owner.
refusals.summary: Decide whether duplicate-key recovery keeps first members for all types

refusals.question: Was the ProtectedOrInternal accessibility change intentional for issue #2234, and if it was accidental, should its correction be handled separately from this fix?
refusals.why: This changes partial-type diagnostic behavior independently of the duplicate-key and mixed-key crash fixes, so it raises a possible regression and a branch/scope decision that I will not make.
refusals.summary: Confirm ProtectedOrInternal was intentional for issue #2234, or handle separately

refusals.question: 6 of 10 new tests pass without the change, so the behaviour they test already works at the base. Does the reported problem exist in this base, and what are these tests for?
refusals.why: Tests that pass with the change reverted: SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.AllowPrivateRequiredIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberTypeMustBeMessagePackObjectIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.MemberWithoutKeyIsReported, SuppressSourceGenerationAnalyzerTests.SourceGenerationOnlyDiagnosticsAreNotReportedWhenSuppressed, SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.NoFormatterIsGeneratedForSuppressedType, SuppressedSourceGenerationTests.SuppressedTypeRoundTripsThroughDynamicResolver
refusals.summary: Confirm whether base reproduces regression and explain six already-passing tests
